cells.tense: You're open to what's arriving and you haven't decided what it means yet.
cells.ask: Tell one person what you noticed before you've sorted it into a conclusion, and let their response sit next to yours without merging the two.
cells.core:
You can take in what's actually here and still keep your feet. The whole shape of something shows up at once, and you let it, and you don't disappear into it. That's not a small thing. Most people either miss the pattern or get swallowed by it. You stay in the room and hold it.

There are feelings moving around you that haven't landed yet — someone's about to say something, something is about to shift — and you don't have to chase any of it early. You can let the next thing come to you. Bring one of those half-formed things to somebody today and stand beside them without becoming them.
cells.sheetLine: You can see the whole thing and stay yourself while you see it.
cells.verb: opening to what's there before knowing what it is
cells.place: where you can see the whole thing from inside it

cells.tense: You're already bracing for how this is going to land before anything has actually happened.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've been preparing a response to and don't respond to it today. Let it finish arriving before you decide what it is.
cells.core:
You're reading the whole thing before it's happened. Some part of you has already mapped how this will go, what they'll feel, what you'll say — and you're living in that version instead of this one. The openness is still there. It's just pointed forward, at a moment that hasn't arrived, which means the actual moment keeps getting missed while you get ready for it.

You don't have to stop seeing ahead. Let something reach you before you've finished handling it. Hold one thing open today without deciding what it is. Whatever wants to be built next will still be buildable — and you'll be building it here instead of somewhere ahead of yourself.

cells.tense: You stopped letting things reach you, and what you can see whole is at some distance now.
cells.ask: Let one small thing touch you today — a song, a face, a moment — and stay with it for a few breaths before you do anything about it.
cells.core:
Seeing a situation whole, from inside it and outside it at once, is a particular thing you can do — read the shape of a room, know how the pieces fit before anyone says them. When you let things reach you while that runs, the pattern keeps filling in. You stay close enough to feel what you're seeing, so what you notice keeps updating instead of setting hard.

What's happening now is that things pass through instead of landing. You can still read the room; the room doesn't reach you. Start with something small — a song you know by heart, one face you see most days — and let it reach you before you've filed it. Stay with it a few breaths without doing anything about it. What you're trying to see whole will come clearer once something can land again.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped letting things reach you, and it made you steadier.

cells.tense: You're already taking things in and seeing how they fit — you'd just never call it that.
cells.ask: Write down one thing you noticed this week that someone else missed, and say what you're going to do with it.
cells.core:
You read rooms. You see how the pieces fit together before anyone says them out loud, and you've been calling that just paying attention, or being the practical one. That seeing is yours. It's running all the time — settling who relaxes, what gets said, what stays unsaid — and it's doing it without getting any credit, including from you.

Someone in the room gets the benefit of it and thinks nothing happened. So does the work that flows through you. You don't have to announce anything. Pick one thing you understood about a situation and claim it as yours — to yourself, out loud, once. That's where the exchange starts, with what you brought.
